title: Check yourself: method references and the types around them

questions.stem: A report keeps its formatters in a `Map<String, Function<Object, String>>`, and registers `formatters.put("secret", String::valueOf)`. A caller then runs `formatters.get("secret").apply(new char[] {'q', '7', 'z'})`. What does it return?

options.text: The text q7z, since the array it receives makes valueOf(char[]) the closest match
options.says: the overload was chosen at compile time from the interface's parameter type, Object; the argument's run-time class plays no part

options.text: The text q7z, since the map's Object type argument is erased by the time apply runs
options.says: the reference was compiled to call valueOf(Object), and nothing at run time changes that choice

options.text: [C@ and a hash, since the reference was compiled against the Object parameter
options.says: Function<Object, String> makes javac resolve String::valueOf as valueOf(Object), which calls the array's toString()

options.text: [C@ and a hash, since String has no valueOf overload that accepts a char[]
options.says: String.valueOf(char[]) exists; a Function<char[], String> target would have chosen it

origin.section: The Interface's Parameter Types Choose the Overload; the Value at Run Time Doesn't

questions.stem: `Indexer` declares a single method `int rebuild()` that returns the number of documents indexed, 5000 in this run. A job runs `Future<?> f = pool.submit(indexer::rebuild);` on an `ExecutorService` and later prints `f.get()`. What happens?

options.text: It prints 5000, since javac prefers the submit overload whose method returns a value
options.says: rebuild has one declaration, so javac can compare the two submit overloads; both fit, and Callable, which returns a value, is more specific

options.text: It prints null, since submit takes every method reference as a Runnable and drops the result
options.says: only a reference to a void method fits Runnable alone; this one also fits Callable, which wins

options.text: It doesn't compile, since rebuild() fits both submit(Runnable) and submit(Callable)
options.says: fitting both is not ambiguous when the reference names one method: the value-returning overload is more specific

options.text: It doesn't compile, since a primitive int can't be the result of a Callable<T>
options.says: the page's int refresh() went through Callable and get() returned 120: the result is boxed

origin.section: An Exact Reference Lets javac Pick `submit(Callable)`; Overloading the Method Makes the Call Ambiguous

questions.stem: Module B calls `pool.submit(mailer::flush)`, where `Mailer` has `int flush()`. A pull request to module A, which owns `Mailer`, adds `int flush(Duration timeout)` and changes nothing else. What happens the next time module B is compiled?

options.text: B fails to compile, since mailer::flush no longer helps javac choose between the submit overloads
options.says: a reference to an overloaded method doesn't take part in choosing submit's overload, both overloads accept it, and the call is ambiguous

options.text: B fails to compile, since mailer::flush now names flush(Duration), which no submit overload can call
options.says: the reference isn't resolved to flush(Duration); javac reports the call to submit as ambiguous

options.text: B compiles and keeps the Callable overload, since only flush() fits an interface without parameters
options.says: that is true of the reference once a target is known, but javac doesn't use it to pick the overload of submit

options.text: B compiles and switches to the Runnable overload, since an overloaded reference is treated as void
options.says: no such rule exists; the call becomes ambiguous and doesn't compile

origin.section: An Exact Reference Lets javac Pick `submit(Callable)`; Overloading the Method Makes the Call Ambiguous

questions.stem: `Ticket` declares `String title()` and `String title(int maxLength)`. A screen sorts with `tickets.sort(Comparator.comparing(Ticket::title).reversed());`, where `tickets` is a `List<Ticket>`. What does javac do?

options.text: It rejects the line, since the reference to title gives comparing no type for its T
options.says: with reversed() called on it, comparing gets no target type, and a reference to an overloaded method tells inference nothing, so T becomes Object

options.text: It rejects the line, since comparing's result can't have reversed() called on it in one expression
options.says: comparing(String::length).reversed() compiles; the chain fails only when the reference gives inference no types

options.text: It accepts the line, since a method reference names its class and so always gives comparing its T
options.says: only a reference to a method with one declaration gives inference its types

options.text: It accepts the line, since title() is the only overload that fits a Function's single parameter
options.says: that holds once the target type is known, but here inference needs T before it can know it

origin.section: An Inexact Method Reference Leaves Inference Without the Types It Needs

questions.stem: A log helper is declared `BiFunction<String, Object, String> log = String::format;`. It is called as `log.apply("%s at %d%%", vals)` with `Object[] vals = {"db-2", 40};`. What happens?

options.text: It returns db-2 at 40%, since the array is passed on as the varargs array
options.says: the array arrives typed Object, and the varargs phase packs it into a new one-element array

options.text: It returns db-2 at 40%, since an Object parameter accepts the array as it is
options.says: accepting the array doesn't spread it; it becomes the single element of the varargs array

options.text: It throws, since the array becomes a single element of a new varargs array
options.says: %s prints the whole array and %d finds no argument: MissingFormatArgumentException

options.text: It throws, since the reference passes only the array's first element to format
options.says: the whole array is passed, as one element; nothing is taken out of it

origin.section: A Varargs Method Packs the Interface's Arguments, So an Array Becomes One Element
